about: Worked examples for CoachNudgePolicy (docs/apps/coach-nudges.md). Each case is a pure input -> expected output: which nudges are emitted, in what order, and which are silent and why. The policy is a pure function, so these are checked without a clock, a database or a network. Edge cases matter more than happy paths: every 'silent' reason exists because a rule would otherwise nag.

schema.now: ISO-8601 local time the policy is evaluated at
schema.signals: the CoachSignals snapshot: baselines, last night, today so far, recent history
schema.ledger: what was already sent / dismissed (fingerprints, per-day counts, per-category gaps, snoozes)

expect.emit: nudge ids in the order they are delivered (first = highest priority)
expect.silent: nudge ids that must NOT be emitted, with the reason (documented per case)
expect.push_count: routine pushes allowed by the policy for this case

cases.why: Resting HR up 12% and sleep 2h under goal: two signals down is A1's threshold, and A1 is the only nudge allowed to push.
One signal down is weather, not a pattern: no nudge.
Six nights is below the 7-night minimum: recovery rules stay silent and Today shows 'Learning your baseline'.
60% of the night recorded is under the 80% floor: nothing is judged.
A very short night alone is A2 (card). With a second signal it becomes A1 and A2 is absorbed, not duplicated.
Recovery beats activity: after A1, B1/B2/B3 stay silent for the rest of the day.
Under 25% of the goal at the check time is B1.

Goal reached at 18:00: B4 fires once and B1/B2 are cancelled for the day. (Corrected 2026-10-20: B4 is a celebration PUSH - policy clause 1 lists it with E2 and F1 - so a day with no routine pushes left still sends it. The original expectation of 0 contradicted the clause.)
21:30 with quiet hours from 22:00: a 'you're 300 steps away' push is noise, so B2 is skipped.
A 7-day streak is a celebration: it does not consume the two routine pushes. (Goal lane disabled: this case is about the streak/review, not about goal-reached.)
The same rounded numbers must not be re-sent: the 15:00 B1 fingerprint was already delivered.
Three activity dismissals in 7 days double the gap to 12h; a nudge inside it is silent even though B1 would otherwise fire.
Two signals down can also be sleep plus last evening's stress, with resting HR at baseline: A1 does not require a heart-rate change.
12% and 2.0 h are the thresholds themselves: the rule is at-or-beyond, so the boundary case fires.
Six nights of history: getting 6/7 of the way to a baseline is not enough, the recovery rules stay silent and Today says 'Learning your baseline'.
79% of the night recorded is below the 80% floor: a mostly-unrecorded night is not judged even when the numbers look bad.
With notifications off every nudge still appears as a Today card: A1 is delivered, it just does not push.
3 h 40 is under the 4 h floor, so A2 fires on the short night alone with every other signal at baseline.
At exactly 2 h under goal with no other signal down, A2 is the card (A1 needs its second signal).
Just under 4 h but two signals down: A1 absorbs the short night, A2 does not also show.
A 3 h night with 55% coverage is a gap in the record, not a short night.

The short-night card was already shown 3 h ago with the same rounded numbers and nothing changed: no repeat inside the 6 h gap. (Vocabulary settled 2026-10-20: one phrase, "already sent today", for every same-day repeat.)
Sleep at 95% of goal with resting HR and last evening's stress at or better than baseline: the green-light card.
89% of the sleep goal misses A3's 90% floor: no 'you're recovered' on an hour of shortfall.
Good sleep and good resting HR are not enough: elevated stress the evening before blocks the green light.
A3 is a card by definition: telling someone they are fine does not earn a notification.
At 12:00 the afternoon has not started: B1 waits for its 15:00 check, so the user is not nagged while there is time.
25% at the check time is not 'behind': the rule is below the fraction, so the boundary stays quiet.
Under 25% but in the middle of a workout: the steps are coming, so no reminder.
A2 fired this morning, so activity stays silent for the rest of the day: recovery beats activity.
The ring only recorded 70% of the day so far: 'you are behind' could be a gap in the record, so nothing is sent.
A nudge that lands inside quiet hours is dropped, never saved for the morning: the 22:00 check window does not survive to 08:00.
92% of the goal after 17:00 with quiet hours 3 h away: the card appears.
84% is below the 85% band: too far to call it 'almost there'.
90% at 15:00 is not B2: earlier in the day there is time to close the ring without a reminder.
20:00 with quiet hours at 22:00 is exactly the 2 h buffer: the boundary is silent.
'Not now' on a B2 pauses the activity category until the next wake time, so the 09:00 card cannot return at 19:00.
No 15-minute block with 250 steps in the last 180 minutes, awake and not training: one movement nudge.
An active block 179 minutes ago is inside the window: not still yet.
B3 already fired at 11:20: a second still-stretch nudge the same day is exactly the nagging the rule avoids.
Asleep at 02:00: no movement reminder, ever. (Recovery topic disabled: this case is about stillness, and a perfect night would otherwise add A3 to the expected list.)
The goal was reached and celebrated at 16:10; a second B4 the same evening would be a duplicate of the same achievement.
Goal already reached: B4 wins the day and B3 stays silent even after three still hours.
Two routine pushes were already used: the celebration still goes out because celebrations have their own slot.
Stress at the user's 82nd percentile and at 64 for 70 minutes with only 120 steps: high for them, and they were not walking it off.
The user's 80th percentile is 55 — below the absolute 60 floor, so a low-percentile user is not nudged about nothing.
High stress by percentile for 70 minutes, but 640 steps in that time: the walking is the answer, no nudge needed.

silent.c1: too many steps during the high stretch

cases.why: 55 minutes of high stress has not yet reached the 60-minute duration.
The follow-up went out 3 h later and stress is still high: a second follow-up is not allowed that day.
One follow-up, 3 h after the first push, and only while stress is still high.

Three of the last seven nights had a bedtime more than 2 h from the user's median: a pattern, worth one push a week. (Recovery topic disabled: this case is about sleep drift, and a perfect night would otherwise add A3 to the expected list.)
Two drifted nights out of seven is a normal week: E1 needs three. (Recovery topic disabled: this case is about sleep drift, and a perfect night would otherwise add A3 to the expected list.)

E1 went out five days ago: a drift is a pattern, and a pattern does not need a reminder every day. (Recovery topic disabled: this case is about sleep drift, and a perfect night would otherwise add A3 to the expected list.)

Only four nights recorded in the window: no median worth calling 'your usual'. (Recovery topic disabled: this case is about sleep drift, and a perfect night would otherwise add A3 to the expected list.)
Steps up 14% over the previous fortnight with 11 of 14 days above the earlier average: a trend, not one big day.

Up 18% but only 7 of 14 days above the earlier average: one long walk is not progress. (Goal lane disabled: this case is about the streak/review, not about goal-reached.) (Celebration lane disabled: a streak is not what this case tests.)

silent.e2: only 7 of 14 days above the earlier average

cases.why: A 6% rise is inside normal week-to-week noise.
Steps were celebrated 9 days ago; the cooldown is 14 days per metric, so the same metric waits.
The steps cooldown does not block sleep: each metric has its own 14-day window.
Three days in a row is the first streak milestone. (Goal lane disabled: this case is about the streak/review, not about goal-reached.)
Four days is not a milestone: the next one is seven. (Goal lane disabled: this case is about the streak/review, not about goal-reached.)
Thirty days fires, and the next milestone is sixty — so thirty-one stays quiet. (Goal lane disabled: this case is about the streak/review, not about goal-reached.)
Notifications off does not hide a streak: it becomes a Today card and a line in the Coach 'For you' list.
Sunday 18:00 is the default review slot and six days of the week have good data: the review is built.

Wednesday is not the review day: one push and one card a week, on the user's chosen slot. (Goal lane disabled: this case is about the streak/review, not about goal-reached.) (Celebration lane disabled: a streak is not what this case tests.)
Four days of good data is below the five-day floor: the review is skipped rather than built from gaps.

Nothing needs fixing this week: the scored recommendation list is empty and the review says keep it up rather than inventing advice. (Goal lane disabled: this case is about the streak/review, not about goal-reached.) (Celebration lane disabled: a streak is not what this case tests.)

A paired ring with no sync for 27 hours: one push a day, and its button opens the ring screen. (Recovery topic disabled: this case is about the ring's sync state, and a perfect night would otherwise add A3 to the expected list.)
No sync for 3 hours is normal between check-ins. (Recovery topic disabled: this case is about the ring's sync state, and a perfect night would otherwise add A3 to the expected list.)

No ring is paired: there is nothing to reconnect, so G1 is not the right nudge. (Recovery topic disabled: this case is about the ring's sync state, and a perfect night would otherwise add A3 to the expected list.)

G1 already fired at 09:00 and the ring is still out of touch: waiting a day beats a push every hour. (Recovery topic disabled: this case is about the ring's sync state, and a perfect night would otherwise add A3 to the expected list.)
Two routine pushes are already out and a third topic is eligible: the limit wins, and the third waits for tomorrow.
The user chose the smallest limit (1): the second routine push of the day is held even though it is eligible.
The user chose the largest limit (3): a third routine push is allowed.
Recovery outranks activity when both are eligible at the same instant: A1 is delivered first and B1 waits. (Phrase settled 2026-10-20: "recovery fired today" is how every case names this merge.)
Stress outranks activity: with both eligible, C1 is the one delivered.
Related nudges merge: the same morning produces one recovery message, not two.
Goal reached merges the activity nudges: B1 and B2 are cancelled for the rest of the day, B4 is the one message.

The fingerprint comes from the ROUNDED STEP COUNT, so 1,204 steps and 1,196 steps round to the same fingerprint (b1:12) and the second is not sent. Same basis as same-fingerprint-never-twice (b1:24) and policy-fingerprint-changes-with-the-number (b1:81).
A materially different number is new information: 1,900 steps is a different fingerprint and may be sent once the gap allows (the last activity push was 6 h 10 m ago, past the 6 h category gap).
The same topic 2 h after a push, no worse: the 6 h gap holds it back.

The gap can be broken only by getting materially worse: 400 steps at 17:30 after 2,200 at 15:00 does not qualify, doubt is resolved by staying silent. (Phrase settled: one sentence for an un-widened category gap.)
Six activity dismissals in seven days take the ladder to 24 h: an eligible B1 inside that gap stays silent.
One tap on an activity nudge resets the ladder: the next eligible B1 goes out at the plain 6 h gap.
'Follow my sleep' moves quiet hours to 23:40–07:10: a 23:50 nudge is dropped by the user's own schedule, not the 22:00 default.

A nudge dropped in quiet hours leaves no fingerprint and no queue entry: nothing arrives at 08:00. (Streak set to 7 so the milestone gate is not the reason - this case is about quiet hours.) (Steps set above the goal so the derived streak really is 7 - the milestone gate is not this case's subject.)
Recovery fired at 07:30, so the whole day stays activity-free even at 15:00 with 800 steps.
With the celebration extra turned off, a celebration push counts against the routine limit and the limit is used up.
Notifications off: nothing is pushed, but A1 is still a Today card and sits in the Coach 'For you' list.
Five nights recorded: 'Learning your baseline' is shown and A1, A2 and A3 are all silent.

A resting HR 40% above baseline is still a wellness comparison: no vitals alarm fires and the wording stays comparative. (No vitals alarm exists anywhere in the product - that is a property, not a silence reason.)

The 'Lighter today' action is only offered as a button on A1/A2 and never applied by itself: with neither fired the goal is untouched. At exactly the check time with 42% of the goal done, B1's reason is the descriptive one (the edge is inclusive), and B3 is inside its window 20 min after an active block.

signals (new keys used by the expansion;.sleep_goal_hours: the user's sleep goal for the night
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.stress_evening_above_normal: last evening's stress above the user's own normal — A1's third signal, and a blocker for A3
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.day_data_percent: share of the day recorded so far, for the 80% floor
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.minutes_since_active_block: minutes since the last 15-min block with >= 250 steps
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.stress_high_minutes: how long stress has sat at or above the higher of the user's 80th percentile and 60
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.stress_percentile_now: the user's percentile of the current reading
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.stress_score_now: the current stress reading (0-100), against the absolute 60 floor
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.drift_nights_last_7: nights (of the last 7) whose bedtime or wake time is > 2 h from the user's median
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.nights_recorded_last_7: nights with enough data inside the drift window
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.improvement_percent: the 14-day window against the 14 days before it
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.days_above_previous: days of the window above the earlier average (need >= 10 of 14)
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.good_days_last_7: days with >= 80% data, for the weekly review's 5-day floor
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.recommendation_candidates: the scored recommendation list; empty means 'keep it up'
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.ring_paired: a ring is paired at all
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.hours_since_sync: hours since the last successful sync
signals (new keys used by the expansion;.previous_fingerprint_value: the number that was in the last fingerprint, to judge 'materially worse'

ledger (new keys).celebration_sent_today: celebration nudge ids already delivered today
ledger (new keys).category_last_sent: per category, the last delivery time
ledger (new keys).category_dismissals_7d: per category, dismissals in the last 7 days
ledger (new keys).snoozed_until: per category, 'Not now' pause end (the user's next wake time)
ledger (new keys).metric_celebrated: per metric, the last E2 delivery
ledger (new keys).notifications_enabled: false = cards and the 'For you' list only
ledger (new keys).quiet_hours: (start, end) when it is not the default
ledger (new keys).sent_today: nudges already delivered today, with their times
